## What it is

Lidarr manages a music collection: it follows your artists, finds new albums through indexers, sends them to a download client and then renames and files them into your library ([Lidarr/Lidarr](https://github.com/Lidarr/Lidarr)).

**Licence:** `GPL-3.0` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L2**. There is no license-matrix row yet, so the gate notes that it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10). The image is built by linuxserver.io ([linuxserver/docker-lidarr](https://github.com/linuxserver/docker-lidarr), GPL-3.0 packaging): Lidarr publishes no image of its own.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): media: music, downloads. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), one container, started as UID 1000 in linuxserver's documented non-root mode (this image is marked `nonroot_supported`), with a writable in-memory `/run` for the s6 supervisor. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volumes: `lidarr-config` (2 GiB, `/config`) and `lidarr-music` (100 GiB, `/music`).
- Probes: `GET /ping`.

## First run

Source: [Servarr wiki, Lidarr Quick Start Guide](https://wiki.servarr.com/lidarr/quick-start-guide).

1. Install Lidarr from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-lidarr`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8686:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-lidarr port-forward svc/lidarr 8686:8686
   ```
3. Set the authentication method and an account when Lidarr asks (Settings, General, Security).
4. Add `/music` as the root folder, then an indexer and a download client. A qBittorrent app on the same box is reachable at `http://qbittorrent.app-qbittorrent.svc:8080`.

## Not done yet

- **Shared downloads:** Lidarr imports finished downloads by reading the download client's files. Each OneMind app has its own volumes in its own namespace, so Lidarr cannot see qBittorrent's `/downloads` yet. Until shared app storage exists, importing finished downloads does not work; searching and sending to the client do.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is not set (linuxserver documents a separate read-only mode; not tested here).
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.
